citation: Scarpel, E., Pettena, A., Cederle, M., Chiariotti, F., Fabris, M., Susto, G.A. (2026) Fully Dynamic Rebalancing in Dockless Bike-Sharing Systems via Deep Reinforcement Learning. arXiv:2605.14501

dedupe_keys.name: bss dynamicrebalancing rl event driven dockless bike sharing simulator with deep reinforcement learning rebalancing

description: BSS-DynamicRebalancing-RL is the code release of a thesis and a 2026 arXiv paper by Edoardo Scarpel and co-authors on fully dynamic rebalancing of dockless bike-sharing systems. A graph-based, event-driven simulator, packaged as a Gymnasium environment, models the service, and a Double Deep Q-Network agent routes a single truck in real time, choosing local pick-up, drop-off and battery charging actions guided by spatiotemporal criticality scores. The repository is a monorepo of five Python packages: preprocessing of trip data into a spatial grid and distance matrices, the simulation environment, training and validation, benchmarks against baseline policies, and a Dash results dashboard, each with a command-line tool. Coverage: Cambridge, Massachusetts, with Bluebikes trip data (September and October 2022 by default), TomTom traffic speed profiles and OpenStreetMap streets; other cities need their own data. Access: code on GitHub; the datasets are not bundled because of their licences, and the preprocessing step downloads them. Licence and cost: MIT, free. Caveats: a research code for one truck and one city, and the README dates the paper to 2025 while arXiv lists May 2026. It supports optimisation and capacity planning of rebalancing operations and fleet size. It relates to FOMOsim, the Capital Bikeshare rebalancing case study and the GBFS specification in the catalogue.
